newsitem.title: MEXICO: BOXING-CHAVEZ CLEARED ON MEXICO TAX-EVASION CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CHAVEZ CLEARED ON MEXICO TAX-EVASION CHARGES.

text.p: Julio Cesar Chavez, one of Mexico's all-time boxing greats, has been cleared of all tax evasion charges, officials said Friday.
A judge in Cuernavaca, just south of Mexico City, on Thursday rescinded the last arrest warrant against Chavez, 33, who was $1.3 million in arrears on his tax bill.
Although Chavez paid off his bills last month, an arrest warrent issued by another judge in the Pacific Coast city of Culiacan had been valid until Thursday.
"The judges suspended the provisional order," Salvador Ochoa, Chavez's lawyer, told reporters.
Chavez was targeted by Finance Ministry officials as part of a high-profile crackdown against tax evasion in Mexico, where less than one-fourth of workers pay their taxes.

By clearing up his problems, Chavez, a three-time world champion with a 98-2-1 record, may attempt a rematch against Mexican-American fighter Oscar de la Hoya in Mexico's huge Aztec Stadium, Ochoa said.
Once one of boxing most fearsome fighters, Chavez has slowed in recent years and lost his World Boxing Council super-lightweight title to De la Hoya on July 6 in Las Vegas.
